title: Unterm — The Best Runtime & Native Assistant for Claude Code, Codex & Agy CLI
excerpt: The pure-Rust GPU terminal built as the best runtime environment and native assistant for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity (agy), and Gemini CLI. Fixes typing lag & dropped keys, TUI tearing, Windows console flashes, multi-agent git conflicts, context-window blind spots, and cross-pane approvals. Local-first, MIT.
content_html:
v0.73.1 · signed + notarized · macOS · Windows · Linux

Traditional terminals were built for single commands—not AI coding CLIs. Unterm solves the 8 biggest native terminal pain points with a pure-Rust GPU core: <2ms zero-drop typing, tear-free TUIs, zero Windows console flashes, isolated Git worktree fleets, live token HUD, and 1-click cross-pane approvals.

WHY UNTERM · PURPOSE-BUILT FOR CLAUDE CODE, CODEX & AGY CLI

8 native terminal pain points when running AI Coding CLIs—solved at the kernel.

Terminal.app, Windows Terminal, iTerm2, and Electron terminals were designed for one command at a time. The moment you run Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Antigravity (agy) all day, every legacy bottleneck surfaces—here is every pain point Unterm eliminates.

PAIN 01 · TYPING LAG, DROPPED KEYS & IME GLITCHES ✓ <2ms input

Under heavy agent output or Windows 15.6ms timer quantization, typing feels sticky, rapid keystrokes drop, and CJK IME compositions get stranded.

Unterm Fix: Dedicated non-blocking coalescing input worker (unterm-input-tx), Windows 1ms timer resolution, DX12 Mailbox 1-frame latency, Win32 WM_CHAR recovery, and automatic orphan IME cleanup.

PAIN 02 · TUI TEARING, FLICKER & BROKEN CHORDS ✓ ?2026 + Kitty

High-frequency TUI redraws tear boxes and flicker, resizing clips wrapped lines, and Shift+Enter accidentally submits prompts instead of inserting newlines.

Unterm Fix: Pure-Rust GPU renderer with global ?2026 synchronized output, main-screen resize reflow, ECMA-48 CJK wide-cell splitting, and Kitty keyboard protocol + modifyOtherKeys.

PAIN 03 · WINDOWS CONSOLE FLASHES & CTRL+C CRASHES ✓ 0 popups

Launching agents, MCP bridges, or background Git probes flashes stray cmd/OpenConsole windows on Windows, and Ctrl+C can drop the background Core.

Unterm Fix: Enforced CREATE_NO_WINDOW across every background subprocess and MCP CLI probe, dedicated hidden-console Ctrl+C helper, and zero-spawn sidebar Git state caching.

PAIN 04 · PARALLEL AGENTS OVERWRITING EACH OTHER ✓ Fleet Arena

Running Claude, Codex, and Agy in the same checkout causes clobbered edits, .git/index.lock failures, and no clean way to compare competing solutions.

Unterm Fix: Native Git Worktree Studio & Fleet Arena: spin up 2–3 agents in isolated worktrees in one click, compare live +added -deleted diffs, and 1-click squash-merge the winner.

PAIN 05 · LOST IN TABS WAITING ON [Y/N] PROMPTS ✓ Cockpit + Mobile

With 6 agents running across tabs, you waste minutes hunting for the pane blocked on an approval prompt—and lose visibility the moment you step away.

Unterm Fix: Live Agent Cockpit status dots, 6-line sidebar hover peeks, Ctrl+Shift+I cross-pane Y/N quick-approve without switching tabs, plus Unterm Pocket QR mobile approvals.

PAIN 06 · CONTEXT OVERFLOW & RE-EXPLAINING WORK ✓ HUD + Handoff

Agents silently hit context limits mid-task, costs scatter across panes, and handing a half-finished task from Claude to Codex means manual copy-paste.

Unterm Fix: Cross-session Daily Telemetry HUD aggregates tokens, USD cost, and success rate; 85%+ context pressure triggers 1-click /compact or portable Handoff (H) to another agent.

PAIN 07 · DIGGING THROUGH LOGS TO FEED AI ✓ OSC 133 + Unzoo

Scrolling up hundreds of lines to drag-select build errors—or copy-pasting browser console crashes back into your CLI agent—breaks your flow constantly.

Unterm Fix: OSC 133 1-click jump to last failed command block, clean output copy, Ctrl+S (✦AI) search-to-agent context feed, plus 1-click Unzoo Browser frontend error self-healing.

PAIN 08 · RISKY AI EDITS & UNSAFE PASTE ✓ Checkpoints + Guard

An agent edits 12 uncommitted files and breaks the build with no clean undo—or a multi-line paste with destructive commands executes immediately on Enter.

Unterm Fix: Zero-pollution hidden Git checkpoints for 1-click rollback, inline Diff single-file revert (Cmd+Shift+G), safe multi-line paste guard, and 3-tier risk-graded autonomy with audit logs.

NATIVE CRAFT · 7 THEMES & HIGH-CONTRAST SPLITS

Unified 36px chrome, sub-millisecond input echo, and unmistakable split-pane focus.

Crafted to macOS HIG and Fluent 2 standards: the active split pane glows with a 2px focus ring and top accent bar while inactive panes softly recede. Click any of the 7 built-in dark & light themes below to preview live.

NEW IN V0.72.0 · NATIVE FLEET ARENA · REMOTE CORE · 165 MCP TOOLS

Parallel Fleet Arena competition, OSC 133 failed-block jump, Search-to-AI context feed, and Remote Core over SSH.

v0.72.0 brings native multi-agent orchestration right into the GPU window: race Claude, Codex, and Agy in isolated Git worktrees, aggregate cross-session token/cost telemetry, attach to remote headless Cores over SSH, and pair over zero-config local MCP with Unzoo Browser.

⚔️ NATIVE FLEET ARENA

Parallel Multi-Agent Arena

Launch 2–3 agents (Claude, Codex, Agy) in parallel isolated worktrees, compare live +added -deleted stats, and 1-click squash-merge the winner while cleaning up the rest.

📜 OSC 133 & SEARCH → AI

Failed-Block Jump & Search-to-AI

Jump directly to the last failed OSC 133 command block or browse recent blocks in-window; press Ctrl+S (✦AI) in the search bar to feed matched context straight to your active agent.

📊 DAILY TELEMETRY HUD

Cross-Session Token & Cost HUD

Aggregates today's token usage, estimated USD cost, peak context occupancy, and task success rate across all active agent panes with 1-click /compact and handoff.

🌐 REMOTE CORE OVER SSH

Remote Core over SSH Tunnels

Run unterm-cli remote-core attach user@host to auto-probe remote core.json, open a keepalive SSH tunnel, and manage remote headless Core sessions from your local GPU window.

🦁 UNTERM × UNZOO BROWSER · THE AI DEVELOPER DUO

Floating 🦁 Unzoo :5173 corner pill & 1-click frontend error self-healing bridge

When a pane starts localhost:3000 / 5173, a floating 🦁 Unzoo :5173 pill appears alongside OSC 133 command duration badges (● Diagnose · exit 1 · 4.2s). Copy clean command output in 1 click (screen.last_command) or bridge Unzoo Browser console errors back to the terminal agent (unzoo.bridge_errors).

Agent cockpit

Three agents, one glance

Stop cycling through tabs to find out who is done. Every row says what its agent is working on, and the one that needs you is marked.

Every tab names its task

Rows read “Add rate limiting to /v1/charge”, not “zsh”. Underneath: which agent, and which branch it is on.

Waiting on you? It comes first

Ctrl Shift A opens the inbox: whoever needs an answer is on top, then what has finished, then what is still running.

Enter, and you are there

Jump straight to the prompt that is waiting, answer it, and go back to what you were doing.

Built to be driven

Your agents can drive the terminal, too

One command registers Unterm with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf and OpenCode. From then on an agent can open tabs, run commands, read the screen and wait for results — through the same 152 MCP methods and 34 CLI commands you can script yourself.

  • Open a tab in the right folder and run the tests
  • Read what a pane printed, or its whole history, as plain text
  • Propose a command you accept with Tab — nothing typed behind your back

Writes into a shell ask for your confirmation until you trust that agent. Everything stays on 127.0.0.1.

Fleets

One task, several agents — keep the best

Hand the same task to Claude and Codex at once. Each works in its own git worktree, so they cannot step on each other or on you.

01

Launch

One command or Ctrl Shift Alt A: a worktree, a branch and a tab for each agent.

02

Compare and check

See each member's diff and run your tests inside its worktree, side by side.

03

Merge the winner

The chosen work lands staged in your repo, uncommitted edits included. You write the commit.

Works with the agents you already use

Install and sign in from inside Unterm, or keep the setup you have. Your subscription stays yours.

Advanced usage

Go further

Recipes you can paste: scripting panes, fleets, recordings, workspaces, per-project identities, raw MCP.

Read the advanced guide →

Frequently asked questions

What is Unterm?

A cross-platform terminal emulator with built-in MCP, HTTP, and CLI control surfaces. The product thesis: terminal as MCP-controllable surface, so any external AI agent can drive it from outside instead of having an AI baked into the terminal itself.

How do I see when Claude Code is waiting for my approval?

Unterm tracks every pane’s agent state. When Claude Code (or Codex, Gemini, Aider) blocks on a confirmation, its tab dot turns amber, the top-bar chip turns amber with a count, and the agent moves to the top of the Agent Inbox (Ctrl+Shift+A) — Enter jumps you straight to that pane. Detection is zero-config for Claude Code and Gemini; “unterm-cli agent enable-hooks” adds exact hook-level reporting.

Can I run multiple Claude Code instances in parallel without them conflicting?

Yes — that is what fleets are for. “unterm-cli fleet launch --agents claude,claude,codex -- task” gives each member its own git worktree and branch beside your repo, so they cannot trample each other or your working copy. Each member gets its own tab with a live state badge, and the Review page compares their results side by side.

How does it work with Claude Code, Cursor, or other agents?

Each Unterm window starts a local MCP server (TCP, JSON-RPC, auth-token gated). Point your MCP client at 127.0.0.1:<port> — the port + token are written to ~/.unterm/server.json on launch. The agent can spawn shells, run commands, read pane state, capture screenshots, toggle recording, and run the Agent Cockpit (status, inbox, fleets, review). Theme, language, and config are deliberately not on MCP; change them in Web Settings, with unterm-cli, or in unterm.conf.

Where does my data go?

Nowhere external. MCP and Web Settings servers bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Session recordings land under <project>/.unterm/sessions/ with built-in redaction for tokens. There is no telemetry, no analytics, no login, no cloud round-trip. Your shell history is yours.

Is there a paid tier or premium feature?

No. Unterm is MIT-licensed; the same single binary ships every feature. No subscription, no Pro tier, no plugin marketplace, no “buy now to unlock split panes.” If you would like to support the project, the Sponsor link in the footer is the only ask.

Which platforms ship signed and notarized?

macOS: universal arm64 + x86_64 DMG signed with a Developer ID and Apple-notarized + stapled (no Gatekeeper warnings). Linux: .deb for Debian/Ubuntu and AppImage for any distro. Windows: WiX-built MSI installer and portable .zip. All published to GitHub Releases on every minor tag.

Is it open-source?

Yes — MIT licensed. The current GUI and terminal runtime use Unterm's native next-core engine, with MCP, Web Settings, recording, i18n, and release tooling in the same repository. Source at github.com/zhitongblog/unterm.

Traditional terminals were built for single commands—not AI coding CLIs. Unterm solves the 8 biggest native terminal pain points with a pure-Rust GPU core: <2ms zero-drop typing, tear-free TUIs, zero Windows console flashes, isolated Git worktree fleets, live token HUD, and 1-click cross-pane approvals.

WHY UNTERM · PURPOSE-BUILT FOR CLAUDE CODE, CODEX & AGY CLI

8 native terminal pain points when running AI Coding CLIs—solved at the kernel.

Terminal.app, Windows Terminal, iTerm2, and Electron terminals were designed for one command at a time. The moment you run Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Antigravity (agy) all day, every legacy bottleneck surfaces—here is every pain point Unterm eliminates.

PAIN 01 · TYPING LAG, DROPPED KEYS & IME GLITCHES ✓ <2ms input

Under heavy agent output or Windows 15.6ms timer quantization, typing feels sticky, rapid keystrokes drop, and CJK IME compositions get stranded.

Unterm Fix: Dedicated non-blocking coalescing input worker (unterm-input-tx), Windows 1ms timer resolution, DX12 Mailbox 1-frame latency, Win32 WM_CHAR recovery, and automatic orphan IME cleanup.

PAIN 02 · TUI TEARING, FLICKER & BROKEN CHORDS ✓ ?2026 + Kitty

High-frequency TUI redraws tear boxes and flicker, resizing clips wrapped lines, and Shift+Enter accidentally submits prompts instead of inserting newlines.

Unterm Fix: Pure-Rust GPU renderer with global ?2026 synchronized output, main-screen resize reflow, ECMA-48 CJK wide-cell splitting, and Kitty keyboard protocol + modifyOtherKeys.

PAIN 03 · WINDOWS CONSOLE FLASHES & CTRL+C CRASHES ✓ 0 popups

Launching agents, MCP bridges, or background Git probes flashes stray cmd/OpenConsole windows on Windows, and Ctrl+C can drop the background Core.

Unterm Fix: Enforced CREATE_NO_WINDOW across every background subprocess and MCP CLI probe, dedicated hidden-console Ctrl+C helper, and zero-spawn sidebar Git state caching.

PAIN 04 · PARALLEL AGENTS OVERWRITING EACH OTHER ✓ Fleet Arena

Running Claude, Codex, and Agy in the same checkout causes clobbered edits, .git/index.lock failures, and no clean way to compare competing solutions.

Unterm Fix: Native Git Worktree Studio & Fleet Arena: spin up 2–3 agents in isolated worktrees in one click, compare live +added -deleted diffs, and 1-click squash-merge the winner.

PAIN 05 · LOST IN TABS WAITING ON [Y/N] PROMPTS ✓ Cockpit + Mobile

With 6 agents running across tabs, you waste minutes hunting for the pane blocked on an approval prompt—and lose visibility the moment you step away.

Unterm Fix: Live Agent Cockpit status dots, 6-line sidebar hover peeks, Ctrl+Shift+I cross-pane Y/N quick-approve without switching tabs, plus Unterm Pocket QR mobile approvals.

PAIN 06 · CONTEXT OVERFLOW & RE-EXPLAINING WORK ✓ HUD + Handoff

Agents silently hit context limits mid-task, costs scatter across panes, and handing a half-finished task from Claude to Codex means manual copy-paste.

Unterm Fix: Cross-session Daily Telemetry HUD aggregates tokens, USD cost, and success rate; 85%+ context pressure triggers 1-click /compact or portable Handoff (H) to another agent.

PAIN 07 · DIGGING THROUGH LOGS TO FEED AI ✓ OSC 133 + Unzoo

Scrolling up hundreds of lines to drag-select build errors—or copy-pasting browser console crashes back into your CLI agent—breaks your flow constantly.

Unterm Fix: OSC 133 1-click jump to last failed command block, clean output copy, Ctrl+S (✦AI) search-to-agent context feed, plus 1-click Unzoo Browser frontend error self-healing.

PAIN 08 · RISKY AI EDITS & UNSAFE PASTE ✓ Checkpoints + Guard

An agent edits 12 uncommitted files and breaks the build with no clean undo—or a multi-line paste with destructive commands executes immediately on Enter.

常见问题

What is Unterm?

A cross-platform terminal emulator with built-in MCP, HTTP, and CLI control surfaces. The product thesis: terminal as MCP-controllable surface, so any external AI agent can drive it from outside instead of having an AI baked into the terminal itself.

How do I see when Claude Code is waiting for my approval?

Unterm tracks every pane’s agent state. When Claude Code (or Codex, Gemini, Aider) blocks on a confirmation, its tab dot turns amber, the top-bar chip turns amber with a count, and the agent moves to the top of the Agent Inbox (Ctrl+Shift+A) — Enter jumps you straight to that pane. Detection is zero-config for Claude Code and Gemini; “unterm-cli agent enable-hooks” adds exact hook-level reporting.

Can I run multiple Claude Code instances in parallel without them conflicting?

Yes — that is what fleets are for. “unterm-cli fleet launch --agents claude,claude,codex -- task” gives each member its own git worktree and branch beside your repo, so they cannot trample each other or your working copy. Each member gets its own tab with a live state badge, and the Review page compares their results side by side.

How does it work with Claude Code, Cursor, or other agents?

Each Unterm window starts a local MCP server (TCP, JSON-RPC, auth-token gated). Point your MCP client at 127.0.0.1:<port> — the port + token are written to ~/.unterm/server.json on launch. The agent can spawn shells, run commands, read pane state, capture screenshots, toggle recording, and run the Agent Cockpit (status, inbox, fleets, review). Theme, language, and config are deliberately not on MCP; change them in Web Settings, with unterm-cli, or in unterm.conf.

Where does my data go?

Nowhere external. MCP and Web Settings servers bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Session recordings land under <project>/.unterm/sessions/ with built-in redaction for tokens. There is no telemetry, no analytics, no login, no cloud round-trip. Your shell history is yours.

Is there a paid tier or premium feature?

No. Unterm is MIT-licensed; the same single binary ships every feature. No subscription, no Pro tier, no plugin marketplace, no “buy now to unlock split panes.” If you would like to support the project, the Sponsor link in the footer is the only ask.

Which platforms ship signed and notarized?

macOS: universal arm64 + x86_64 DMG signed with a Developer ID and Apple-notarized + stapled (no Gatekeeper warnings). Linux: .deb for Debian/Ubuntu and AppImage for any distro. Windows: WiX-built MSI installer and portable .zip. All published to GitHub Releases on every minor tag.

Is it open-source?

Yes — MIT licensed. The current GUI and terminal runtime use Unterm's native next-core engine, with MCP, Web Settings, recording, i18n, and release tooling in the same repository. Source at github.com/zhitongblog/unterm.
